about: The Marian antiphon of Paschaltide: from Compline of Holy Saturday until the Saturday after Pentecost it stands where the Ave Regína cælorum stood through Lent — and the Salve Regína will stand again from Trinity Sunday. Its author is unknown and the text is attested by the twelfth century. Since Benedict XIV it also replaces the Angelus through the Easter season, and is said standing — the Church does not kneel for prayer in these weeks. Four short lines, each sealed with an alleluia: the first calls for joy, the next two give the reason for it — and the main verb that sentence waits on arrives only at the opening of the third line — and the fourth asks. A versicle and its answer follow.

s02.translation: for He whom you did merit to bear, alleluia,

s03.translation: has risen, as He said, alleluia.

s04.translation: Pray to God for us, alleluia.

s05.translation: Rejoice and be glad, O Virgin Mary, alleluia.

s06.translation: For the Lord has truly risen, alleluia.

w002.function: Genitive with “Regína” (w001): queen of what — of heaven.

w003.function: The imperative of a deponent verb: passive in form, active in meaning — rejoice, not be rejoiced.

w005.function: Opens the reason to rejoice: the two lines that follow are the ground of the command “lætáre” (w003).

w006.function: Accusative, the object of “portáre” (w008). The antiphon never names the one it speaks of — it identifies him by what he did.

w007.function: Second person: the antiphon is addressing Mary directly. With an infinitive, liturgical “meruísti” means to be granted something rather than to have earned it.

w008.function: Infinitive depending on “meruísti” (w007) — worthy to bear him.

w010.function: The verb the sentence was holding back for “quem” (w006): the subject is the one she bore.

w012.function: The same subject as “Resurréxit” (w010): he had said it of himself.

w014.function: Imperative: the antiphon turns from rejoicing to asking.

w016.function: Ablative after “pro” (w015): those on whose behalf the prayer is made.

w017.function: Accusative, the object of “Ora” (w014): Latin oráre governs the one entreated in the accusative. So the line asks God on our behalf — it does not ask for God.

w019.function: An active imperative standing beside the deponent “lætáre” (w021), which says the same thing in passive form.

w023.function: Vocative. The versicle names Mary, to whom the antiphon is addressed.

w026.function: Without the re- of “Resurréxit” (w010), though it speaks of the same rising.

w027.function: Nominative, and the subject stated at last: through “quem” (w006) and “Resurréxit” (w010) the antiphon spoke of him without once saying who he was.
